free_tier.stated: When you create a new AWS Free Tier account, you get $100 in credits immediately. As you explore key services, you can earn up to $100 more. That's up to $200 over 6 months to build, break things, and experiment with no charges and no surprise bills on the Free plan. The account closes on its own 6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first.

egress.terms: AWS customers receive 100 GB of free data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud).; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: AWS customers receive 100 GB of free data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud).

interface_detail: SSH to the instance's public IPv4 or IPv6 address, with a security group rule for any further port
chaining: 100 GB a month is a signalling or control-plane allowance, not a data path; it does not compose into a 1 TiB a month chain at any price of zero

limits.value: 100 GB of data transfer out to the internet each month, aggregated across services and regions
the Free plan account closes 6 months after creation or when credits run out

binding_note: 100 GB a month is 3.33 GB a day, 9.1% of 1 TiB a month, so a run at a 1 TiB/month pace exhausts the allowance in about 2.7 days; the 6-month account closure sits behind it and would matter only to an idle account

identity_cost.detail: unverified on the pages read: neither aws.amazon.com/free nor its FAQ states the signup instrument, so a card is recorded as the expected instrument and not as a quoted term

reliability_note: the Free plan closes the account 6 months after creation or when the credits run out, whichever comes first; nothing in the pages read says an EC2 instance survives that
confidence_note: the 100 GB line and the 6-month plan are on AWS pages read today; the identity instrument and any per-service hour allowance are not, so those parts stay unverified

evidence.proved: 'AWS customers receive 100 GB of free data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud).'
'up to $200 over 6 months ... The account closes on its own 6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first.'
'The free plan is available for 6 months after account creation' and no 750-hour figure on the EC2 product page
a security group rule names protocol 17 (UDP) and a single port, so UDP ingress is expressible and 51820 is not special

price_per_tb_month: USD 0 on the Free plan for 6 months; the 100 GB a month egress allowance is free on every account
notes: The 750 hours for 12 months that was asked to confirm is not on any page read today: aws.amazon.com/free, its free-tier FAQ, the EC2 product page and the EC2 on-demand pricing page all describe USD 200 of credits over a 6-month Free plan, and none carries a per-service hour allowance. The offer appears to have been restructured around credits; whether a 750-hour line survives on a page not read is open, and the pages read do not support the claim. The 100 GB allowance is separate from the plan and is standing for all customers.

extras.wg_detail: a security group rule takes a protocol number and a port range: 'The most common protocols are 6 (TCP), 17 (UDP), and 1 (ICMP)' and 'For TCP, UDP, or a custom protocol, the range of ports to allow. You can specify a single port number (for example, 22)', so 51820/udp is one rule and wg-quick runs natively
extras.volume_stated: AWS customers receive 100 GB of free data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud).
extras.transit_note: bytes leave through the instance's public address and are aggregated with every other AWS service's egress into the same 100 GB
